answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers cap each identity at one answer per epoch. Registering locks a 100-coin bond and a secret key split into shares. Each answer publishes one share tied to the epoch seed; a second answer in the same epoch exposes another share, so anyone can rebuild the key and slash the bond. A farm of 500 fakes must lock 50,000 coins, each bond separate and not poolable, so its returns hit a nadir after one slip. Sybils stay a faint nebula of single answers, and a dune of locked coins sits idle.
